# Browser automation (OpenCode Browser v2)

Use these tools whenever a task needs the browser instead of plain HTTP fetching:
signed-in pages, SPAs, dashboards, form submission, screenshots, or anything that
requires a real JavaScript environment with the user's cookies.

## Workflow

1. `browser_list` — see open tabs and get `target_id`s. **Prefer an existing tab.**
2. `browser_snapshot` — get the accessibility tree with `[uid]` markers.
3. Act with `browser_click` / `browser_fill` using UIDs from the **latest** snapshot.
4. Verify with `browser_snapshot` or `browser_eval` after each action.
5. Use `browser_new_tab` only when there is no suitable tab, and clean up with
   `browser_close_tab` when done.

## Rules

- Never close or navigate a tab the user is actively working in without asking.
- The snapshot UID space resets on every `browser_snapshot` call — always re-snapshot
  before clicking or filling, and pass the same `target_id` to every call.
- `browser_url` defaults to the local bridge (`http://127.0.0.1:9333`). Leave it unset
  unless the user configured a different endpoint.
- If tools return `HTTP 503`, the user has not enabled
  `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` in Chrome yet.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `browser_list` | List tabs (targets) |
| `browser_new_tab` | Open a new tab (no popup blocking) |
| `browser_close_tab` | Close a tab you opened |
| `browser_navigate` | Navigate a tab to a URL |
| `browser_snapshot` | Accessibility tree with UIDs |
| `browser_click` | Click by snapshot UID |
| `browser_fill` | Fill an input by snapshot UID |
| `browser_eval` | Evaluate JavaScript in the page |
| `browser_screenshot` | Capture a PNG |
| `browser_version` | Show the plugin version |

# OpenCode Browser v2 **Chrome browser automation for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 2 — control your *real* browser from the agent.** Tabs · Navigation · Accessibility snapshots · Clicks · Form filling · JavaScript eval · Screenshots — over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, no browser extension required. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![OpenCode v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-v2-7C3AED.svg)](https://opencode.ai) [![Chrome 144+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome-144%2B-4285F4.svg?logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.google.com/chrome/) [![Protocol](https://img.shields.io/badge/protocol-CDP-orange.svg)](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/) [![Node >= 20](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-339933.svg?logo=node.js&logoColor=white)](https://nodejs.org) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](#contributing) A V2-ready fork of [different-ai/opencode-browser](https://github.com/different-ai/opencode-browser) — ported to the OpenCode 2 plugin API, with real bug fixes and new tab management tools.
--- ## Table of contents - [Why this fork](#why-this-fork) - [Features](#features) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Tools reference](#tools-reference) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Using your real Chrome profile](#using-your-real-chrome-profile) - [Manual installation](#manual-installation) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Security](#security) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Why this fork The original [opencode-browser](https://github.com/different-ai/opencode-browser) is an excellent Chrome automation plugin — but it targets the **OpenCode 1 plugin API**. OpenCode 2 intentionally changed the plugin contract, and V1 plugin implementations **do not load** in V2 (you get `Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function`). This project is a drop-in replacement for OpenCode 2 users. It: - ✅ **Ports the plugin to the OpenCode V2 API** (`Plugin.define` + `ctx.tool.transform`), exposing all tools natively to the agent (`options.codemode: false`). - 🐛 **Fixes the accessibility snapshot bug** — the original walker discarded ignored AX subtrees, so `browser_snapshot` returned only the page root on most sites and `browser_click`/`browser_fill` could never resolve a UID. Snapshots now contain the full tree. - 🐛 **Fixes screenshots hanging on background tabs** — `Page.bringToFront` is issued before capture. - 🆕 **Adds tab management**: `browser_new_tab` (works even where `window.open` is popup-blocked, because it uses the DevTools protocol) and `browser_close_tab`. - 🧹 **Drops the external dependency chain** in the tool layer — the tools use the built-in `fetch` and `WebSocket` only. - 🔌 **Ships a tiny local bridge** that makes the plugin work with your **everyday Chrome profile** (tabs, cookies, logins) despite Chrome 136+'s remote-debugging hardening — see [Using your real Chrome profile](#using-your-real-chrome-profile). ## Features - **Drive the browser the user actually uses** — your tabs, your sessions, your logins. - **10 first-class agent tools** for listing tabs, navigating, snapshotting, clicking, filling, evaluating JavaScript and capturing screenshots. - **Accessibility-tree snapshots** with stable `[uid]` markers for reliable clicking and typing. - **No Chrome extension, no native messaging host, no broker** — direct CDP over local HTTP + WebSocket. - **Works with Chrome, Chromium, Electron and remote/proxied CDP endpoints** — any endpoint reachable over `/json/*`. - **Safe by default**: the bridge binds to `127.0.0.1`, and real-profile access still requires a per-session Chrome toggle and Allow prompt. ## Requirements | Requirement | Notes | |---|---| | OpenCode v2.0.32+ | V2 plugin API | | Node.js ≥ 20 | for the local bridge and the plugin runtime | | Chrome / Chromium 144+ | for the `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` toggle (older versions work with `--remote-debugging-port` instead) | | Linux, macOS or Windows | the plugin is cross-platform; the installer auto-starts the bridge via systemd on Linux only | ## Quick start ```bash # 1. Clone git clone https://github.com/HadiAlizade77/opencode-browser-v2.git cd opencode-browser-v2 # 2. Install (plugin + bridge + service + config entry, with backup) ./scripts/install.sh # 3. Enable remote debugging in Chrome (once per browser start) # open chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging and switch it on # 4. Restart OpenCode ``` Then try: ```text List my browser tabs, open example.com in a new tab, take a screenshot and close it. ``` ## Tools reference | Tool | What it does | Key parameters | |---|---|---| | `browser_list` | Lists page targets (tabs) with IDs, titles and URLs | `browser_url` | | `browser_new_tab` | Opens a new tab via CDP — popup blockers never apply | `url` (default `about:blank`) | | `browser_close_tab` | Closes a tab by target ID | `target_id` | | `browser_navigate` | Navigates a tab and waits for load | `url`, `target_id` | | `browser_snapshot` | Accessibility tree with `[uid]` markers for click/fill | `target_id` | | `browser_click` | Clicks an element by snapshot UID (real mouse events, JS fallback) | `uid`, `target_id` | | `browser_fill` | Clears and fills an input by snapshot UID (native setter + `Input.insertText`) | `uid`, `value`, `target_id` | | `browser_eval` | Evaluates JavaScript in the page and returns the value | `expression`, `target_id` | | `browser_screenshot` | Saves a PNG screenshot and returns its path | `target_id` | | `browser_version` | Reports the installed plugin version | — | All tools accept an optional `browser_url`. It defaults to the local bridge (`http://127.0.0.1:9333`), and to `OPENCODE_BROWSER_URL` when set. ## How it works ```text ┌────────────────────┐ native tools ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ OpenCode 2 │ ────────────────▶ │ opencode-browser-v2 plugin │ │ agent │ │ (V2 API, no dependencies) │ └────────────────────┘ └──────────────┬──────────────┘ │ HTTP + WebSocket (CDP) ┌───────────▼────────────┐ │ bridge 127.0.0.1:9333 │ └───────────┬────────────┘ │ browser WebSocket ┌───────────▼────────────┐ │ Chrome (your profile) │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` - The **plugin** registers the ten tools and speaks CDP: `/json/list`, `/json/new`, `/json/close/` for discovery and one WebSocket per tab for commands. - The **bridge** exists for one reason: since Chrome 136, Chrome ignores `--remote-debugging-port` for the default profile, and the sanctioned `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` toggle (Chrome 144+) exposes **only a WebSocket** — no `/json` HTTP endpoints. The bridge reads `DevToolsActivePort`, keeps one browser-level WebSocket to Chrome, and presents a standard CDP-looking HTTP surface on `127.0.0.1:9333` that the plugin understands. If you launch Chrome yourself with `--remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=` (a dedicated automation profile), you don't need the bridge at all — pass `browser_url: "http://127.0.0.1:9222"` and the tools talk to Chrome directly. ## Using your real Chrome profile Chrome deliberately blocks remote debugging on the default profile. The supported path is Chrome's own toggle: 1. In Chrome, open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging`. 2. Enable **Remote debugging**. Chrome shows a permission dialog the first time an agent connects — click **Allow**. 3. Keep Chrome open. After a full browser restart, enable the toggle again. That's it — the agent can now see and drive the tabs you already have open, with your existing logins. The bridge auto-detects the standard Chrome, Chromium, Brave and Edge user-data directories on Linux, macOS and Windows. If your browser keeps its profile elsewhere, set `CHROME_PROFILE_DIR` to that directory. > **Alternative:** run a dedicated debug profile instead of your real one: > `google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="$HOME/.config/opencode/chrome-profile"` > and point tools at `http://127.0.0.1:9222`. No toggle, no permission prompt, separate sessions. ## Manual installation
Prefer to do it by hand? Click to expand. **1. The plugin** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-chrome-devtools cp src/index.ts src/lib.js ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-chrome-devtools/ ``` **2. The config entry** (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ "/home/YOU/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-chrome-devtools" ] } ``` **3. The bridge** (only needed for the real-profile toggle route) ```bash mkdir -p ~/.local/share/opencode-chrome-bridge ~/.local/bin npm install --prefix ~/.local/share/opencode-chrome-bridge ws@8 cp bridge/opencode-chrome-bridge.js ~/.local/bin/ NODE_PATH=~/.local/share/opencode-chrome-bridge/node_modules \ node ~/.local/bin/opencode-chrome-bridge.js ``` For autostart on Linux, copy `bridge/opencode-chrome-bridge.service` to `~/.config/systemd/user/`, replace `__NODE_BIN__` with the absolute path of your `node` binary (`command -v node`), `__BRIDGE_JS__` and `__NODE_PATH__` with your paths, then: ```bash systemctl --user daemon-reload systemctl --user enable --now opencode-chrome-bridge.service ``` On macOS/Windows, start the same command via your login items / Task Scheduler.
## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause & fix | |---|---| | `HTTP 503 — Enable remote debugging first` | The Chrome toggle is off. Open `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and enable it. | | `Target … not found` | The tab was closed since you listed it. Call `browser_list` again. | | `No snapshot cached. Call browser_snapshot first.` | Snapshot UIDs expire per call; re-run `browser_snapshot` before click/fill. | | Tools missing from the agent | Restart OpenCode; check `plugins` in `opencode.json` points at the plugin directory. | | `EADDRINUSE` on 9333 | Another bridge instance is running: `systemctl --user restart opencode-chrome-bridge`. | | `env: 'node': No such file or directory` in the journal | The systemd user session cannot see your Node install (nvm/fnm/asdf/volta). Re-run `./scripts/install.sh`, which pins the absolute node path in `ExecStart`; the old installer used `/usr/bin/env node`. | | Permission dialog keeps appearing | Chrome asks per debug session; click **Allow**. Restarting Chrome resets the toggle. | | Screenshot is blank/slow | The plugin brings the tab to front first; if a page renders lazily, wait and retry. | Logs: `journalctl --user -u opencode-chrome-bridge -f` ## FAQ **Can OpenCode control my browser?** Yes — this plugin gives the OpenCode 2 agent ten browser tools: list tabs, open/close tabs, navigate, snapshot the accessibility tree, click, fill forms, run JavaScript and take screenshots. It drives your real, logged-in Chrome. **Does it need a Chrome extension?** No. It speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol over local HTTP + WebSocket. Nothing is installed into Chrome itself. **Why does `--remote-debugging-port` no longer work with my normal profile?** Chrome 136 hardened remote debugging: the flag is ignored for the default profile, and Chrome 144+ provides the `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` toggle instead. This project's bridge implements the missing HTTP layer for that toggle so existing CDP tooling keeps working. **Can the agent see my logins and cookies?** Only within the tabs it's allowed to attach to, and only while you keep the Chrome toggle enabled and have clicked Allow. Nothing leaves your machine. **Which browsers are supported?** Chrome and Chromium (including Edge), Electron apps that expose a CDP endpoint, and remote/proxied CDP endpoints — anywhere `/json/list` and page WebSockets are reachable. **Does it work on Windows/macOS?** The plugin and bridge are plain Node.js and run anywhere. The bundled installer's service autostart is Linux/systemd; elsewhere start the bridge via login items or Task Scheduler. **How is this different from the original opencode-browser?** It's a V2 port (the original targets OpenCode 1 and won't load in V2), plus fixes for the snapshot subtree bug and background-tab screenshots, plus `browser_new_tab`/`browser_close_tab`, plus the real-profile bridge. ## Security - The bridge listens on `127.0.0.1` only, and every CDP connection stays on your machine. - Real-profile access is gated by Chrome itself: the agent cannot attach until you enable `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and approve the connection. - Treat the debug port and the toggle as sensitive: anyone who can reach the endpoint can control the browser. Don't expose it beyond localhost. - The bridge keeps a single browser-level WebSocket so the permission prompt appears as rarely as Chrome allows. ## Project layout ```text opencode-browser-v2/ ├── src/ │ ├── index.ts # OpenCode V2 plugin wrapper (Plugin.define) │ └── lib.js # the ten tools + CDP client + snapshot walker ├── bridge/ │ ├── opencode-chrome-bridge.js # CDP HTTP/WS bridge for the real-profile toggle │ └── opencode-chrome-bridge.service ├── scripts/ │ └── install.sh # one-shot installer (plugin + bridge + config) └── .opencode/skill/browser-automation/SKILL.md # optional agent skill ``` ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. If you found a bug in the *original* V1 plugin (`different-ai/opencode-browser`) that also applies here, please report it [there](https://github.com/different-ai/opencode-browser/issues) as well — this fork prefers to stay a thin, well-documented layer on top. ## Credits - Original project: [different-ai/opencode-browser](https://github.com/different-ai/opencode-browser) by Benjamin Shafii and contributors (MIT). - Inspired by Claude in Chrome. - Built on the [Chrome DevTools Protocol](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Hadi Alizadeh — includes portions of the original project © 2025 different-ai / Benjamin Shafii.
